records.name: THORPE FARMHOUSE
records.details:
TL08SW
7/133
23/05/67

THORPE ACHURCH
THORPE WATERVILLE
Thorpe Farmhouse

(Formerly listed as Thorpe Waterville Farmhouse)

GV
II

Farmhouse, now house. Late C17 and early C19. Squared coursed limestone with
Collyweston slate roof. Originally 3-unit plan. 2 storeys with attic. Main
front is a 3-window range. 2-window range to left, remodelled and raised early
C19. Central panelled door with arch-head fanlight set in wooden surround.
Tripartite sash windows with glazing bars under gauged stone heads with ashlar
dressings. Ashlar gable parapet and truncated ashlar stacks at ends. One-window
range to right is late C17 with 3-light stone mullion windows with hood mould.
Similar 2-light window to far left at ground floor and part-glazed door, to
right, under wood lintel. Late C17 range has lower eaves, and ridge. Ashlar
gable parapets and ashlar stack abutting early C19 roof. Quoins between C17 and
C19 ranges are stuccoed. Right gable has 2-light stone mullion attic window.
Rear elevation has C20 extension and one roof dormer with leaded casement.
Interior not inspected.

Listing NGR: TL0235181594

records.name: CASTLE BARN APPROXIMATELY 50 METRES NORTH EAST OF THORPE CASTLE HOUSE
records.officialName: Castle Barn Approximately 50 Metres North East of Thorpe Castle House
records.details:
THORPE ALCHURCH THORPE WATERVILLE TL08SW Castle Barn approx. 50m. 7/135 NE of Thorpe Castle House 23/05/67 (Formerly listed as Castle Barn) GV I

Great hall of castle, now a barn. Early C14 origins for Walter de Langton. Bishop of Lichfield. Squared coursed limestone with thatch roof. Rectangular plan, originally probably the hall and solar range. Originally part 2 storeys, first floor structure now removed. West elevation has central C19 cart entrance. Ashlar plinth. Ashlar gable parapets. Gable to left has projecting chimney breast, corbelled out from first floor level, and eith octagonal crenellated flue on square base. At attic level the chimney breast is flanked by deeply recessed circcular windows with moulded surrounds. Right gable has slit vents. Rear has C19 central cart entrance. Interior: very fine king-post roof structure. Tie beams have wall posts and curved braces, the king posts have braces in both directions, and similar braces opposite the collars. Main beams have moulded soffits. Moulded cornice. Evidence of screen in roof structure of bay to north. Evidence of first floor fireplace in north gable wall. Roof structure of hall range has smoke blackening. A 2-storey gabled porch is said to have been removed C19. Walter de Langton was licensed to crenellate in 1301. (Buildings of England:Northanptonshire, p. 429; V.C.H. : Northamptonshire, Vol.5, p.135).

Listing NGR: TL0225881433

records.name: BRIDGE AT TL 0227 8128
records.details:
TL08SW A605

4/185

Bridge at TL 0227 8128
- II

Road bridge. Probably early C14, widened late C18. Limestone ashlar. Single
span. C18 semi-circular outer arches. Low parapets have plain ashlar plinth. C14
chamfered ribs in centre of bridge, 3 are straight and 2 are oblique.
(Buildings of England: Northamptonshire, p.429).

The asset was previously listed twice also under the parish of Thorpe Achurch at List entry 1040141. This entry was removed from the List on 10 November 2017.

records.name: THORPE CASTLE HOUSE
records.details:
TL08SW
7/134
23/05/67

THORPE ACHURCH
THORPE WATERVILLE
Thorpe Castle House

(Formerly listed as Castle Farmhouse, now 2 cottages)

GV II

Manor house. Probably medieval origins as part of Thorpe Waterville Castle.
Mainly mid C17, restored C19 and C20. Squared coursed limestone with
Collyweston slate roof. Irregular T-shape plan. 2 storeys with attic. Entrance
front of 4 bays with later gabled cross wing breaking forward to right of
centre. Doorway to right of cross wing has 4-centred arch head with mouldings to
topside of lintel, probably reset. C20 door. C19 two- and 3-light stone mullion
windows, above door, and to first floor and attic. C20 two-light stone mullion
window to ground floor left of cross wing with single-light window above. C19
two-light stone mullion window with transom to first floor right. Return walls
of cross wing have single-light windows. Lateral stone stacks to left and right.
Ashlar gable parapets, cross wing has crow stepped gable. Elevation to right of
entrance front is a 2-window range of C20 stone mullion windows with gable to
left. Reset medieval lancet window to first floor left of gable. Rear elevation
has projecting wing to left, probably C19. Central gabled attic dormer has
lateral stack attached to right. C20 stone mullioned bay window to right. Ashlar
gable parapets and stone stacks at ridge and end. The house may incorporate some
remains of Thorpe Waterville Castle of which Castle Barn approximately 50 metres
north-east of Thorpe Castle House (q.v.) is the chief survival. Probably
converted to 2 farm cottages late C18. Interior not inspected but said to be
remodelled C20.
(Buildings of England: Northamptonshire, p.429; V.C.H.: Northamptonshire, Vol.3,
p.135).

Listing NGR: TL0222581402

records.name: POST BOX COTTAGE
records.details:
THORPE ACHURCH THORPE WATERVILLE TL08SW 7/132 Post Box Cottage GV II

House. Late C17 and C20. Regular coursed limestone with thatch roof. Orignally 2-unit plan. Single storey with attic. 3-window range of C20 casements under wood lintels, 2 are renewed. Fire window to far right. 3 C20 leaded casements to attic under eyebrow dormers. Ashlar gable parapets and kneelers and brick and stone stacks at ends. Entrance in C20, single storey, extension to rear. Interior: room to right has open fireplace with bressumer. Stud screen at first floor with wattle infill panels. Included for group value.

Listing NGR: TL0234881558
